$comment: THE SERVER LIST. Every other copy of it is generated from this file by
`make servers` (scripts/generate-servers.mjs), and CI fails if any of them
has drifted. This is the `surfaces.json` pattern from cupertino, applied to
the thing Bastion actually supervises.
v1 is a CLOSED LIST. Bastion spawns manifest-listed servers and nothing
else — no catalog, no arbitrary code. That is a security property, not a
roadmap gap: the catalog is a solved, free problem (Docker MCP Toolkit,
MCPB, the official registry) and the defensible part is the runtime.
Adding a server: add an entry here, run `make servers`, review the diff.
Nothing below is free-form — scripts/servers.schema.json is enforced by the
generator before it writes anything.
Field notes, for the fields whose reason is not obvious:
distribution  Where the code comes from. Only three of these are on npm
today; the rest are private checkouts under the mgcrea-ai
directory, and `localPath` names the checkout. Bastion
prefers npm when it is there because a published tarball is
the thing users can actually get.
dialect       The NEWEST protocol version the server itself speaks, which
is not the one Bastion fronts clients with. Measured, not
assumed: every one of these runs @modelcontextprotocol/sdk
1.29 or 1.30, whose LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25,
and a live `initialize` handshake against mcp-shopify
negotiates exactly that. The first version of this file said
2025-06-18 for all ten, which was Bastion's own pin
masquerading as a fact about the servers, and would have
given up a year of protocol for nothing.
Every value here is a LEGACY (handshake) version. The
2026-07-28 spec calls a server “modern” when it takes
version, identity and capabilities as per-request `_meta`,
and “legacy” when it wants an `initialize` handshake. None
of these are modern: `server/discover` against mcp-shopify
returns -32601, which is precisely the fallback signal the
spec names.
writeGate     The env var that turns destructive tools on. Per PROFILE in
Bastion, never global — that is the answer to the third
reason cupertino's ServerHost.swift gives for one process
per connection. A null gate means the server has no write
path at all, which is what makes shopify the right first
end-to-end target.
authModes     Several of these accept more than one credential shape and
infer which one from what is set. A profile must fill
exactly one mode; the env entries in a mode are therefore
required:false individually and validated as a group.
stateEnv      Env vars naming ON-DISK STATE. These are the reason a naive
singleton is wrong: two profiles of mcp-reddit sharing one
token file are two identities sharing one login. Bastion
redirects each of these into the profile's own directory.
portEnv       Env vars naming a LISTENING PORT the server opens for its
own OAuth callback. Two profiles of the same server collide
on the default; Bastion assigns per-profile ports and
rewrites the matching redirect URI.

servers.summary: Shopify Admin GraphQL API: products, variants, collections, metafields, locations.

env.name: SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN
env.description: Store handle or *.myshopify.com domain. A bare handle is expanded.

env.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Custom app client id.

env.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Custom app client secret. Used as the Admin API access token.

env.name: SHOPIFY_API_VERSION
env.description: Admin API version, e.g. 2026-04. Defaults to the server's pinned version.

notes: No write gate because there is no write path: every tool is a read.
That is why the build order takes this one end-to-end first — a bug in
the supervisor or the dialect layer cannot cost anybody data here.

servers.summary: App Store Connect API: apps, versions, builds, TestFlight, listings, analytics, sales.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID
env.description: The 10-character API key id.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID
env.description: Issuer UUID from the Keys page.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_P8
env.description: The .p8 private key, inline PEM. Preferred: Bastion keeps it in the Keychain and never writes it to disk.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_P8_PATH
env.description: Path to a .p8 file on disk. The legacy shape — it leaves the key readable outside the Keychain.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_VENDOR_NUMBER
env.description: Vendor number, needed only for sales and finance reports.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables the mutating tools: version metadata, screenshots, submissions, pricing.

notes: The inline key is why `secret` is a manifest field rather than a UI
guess. `.mcp.json` in mcp-appstore-connect currently holds this key in
plaintext; migrating it into a Bastion profile is the first dogfood
task in the build order.

servers.summary: Keycloak Admin REST API: realms, clients, users, roles, sessions.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_URL
env.description: Base URL of the Keycloak server, e.g. https://sso.example.com.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_REALM
env.description: Realm to administer. Defaults to master.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_AUTH_REALM
env.description: Realm to authenticate against, when it differs from the one being administered.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Client id. Defaults to admin-cli.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Client secret. Selects the client_credentials grant.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_USERNAME
env.description: Admin username. Selects the password grant.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_PASSWORD
env.description: Admin password.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables creating and modifying realms, clients, users and roles.

notes: The profile split is the whole point here: rgis and ivalis are two
realms on two servers with two admin identities, and a single global
instance could hold only one of them.

servers.summary: OVHcloud API, focused on Object Storage: containers, objects, policies, regions.

env.name: OVH_ENDPOINT
env.description: Region endpoint: ovh-eu, ovh-ca, ovh-us. Defaults to ovh-eu.

env.name: OVH_CLIENT_ID
env.description: OAuth2 client id.

env.name: OVH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth2 client secret.

env.name: OVH_APPLICATION_KEY
env.description: Application key, from https://eu.api.ovh.com/createToken/.

env.name: OVH_APPLICATION_SECRET
env.description: Application secret.

env.name: OVH_CONSUMER_KEY
env.description: Consumer key, which carries the granted scopes.

env.name: OVH_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A pre-minted access token.

env.name: OVH_CLOUD_PROJECT
env.description: Default public cloud project id, a 32-character hex string.

env.name: OVH_REGION
env.description: Default storage region, e.g. GRA, SBG, UK.

env.name: OVH_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables uploading, deleting and re-policying objects and containers.

notes: Three auth modes, inferred from what is set. The signature triplet is
the only one of the three where every part is a secret, which is
exactly the sort of detail a hand-written profile form gets wrong.

servers.summary: Reddit API: subreddits, posts, comments, search, and the user's own history.

env.name: REDDIT_CLIENT_ID
env.description: App client id. Anonymous app-only reads work without it; anything user-scoped does not.

env.name: REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: App client secret. Empty for an installed app, set for a web or script app.

env.name: REDDIT_USER_AGENT
env.description: platform:app-id:version (by /u/username). Reddit throttles generic agents regardless of rate limit.

env.name: REDDIT_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: Loopback OAuth callback. Per-profile, or two profiles race for one port — and the URL must be registered with the Reddit app.

env.name: REDDIT_TOKEN_PATH
env.description: Where the refresh token is stored. Per-profile, or two profiles share one login.

env.name: REDDIT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables posting, commenting and voting.

notes: The clearest case for stateEnv and portEnv. This server logs a user in
over a local callback and keeps the refresh token in a file — both of
which are per-identity, so both must be per-profile.

servers.summary: X (Twitter) API v2: posts, threads, timelines, search, bookmarks, and the Ads API.

env.name: X_API_BEARER_TOKEN
env.description: App-only bearer token. Reads only; the Ads API rejects it outright.

env.name: X_API_CLIENT_ID
env.description: OAuth2 client id. Required for a user context, and therefore for writes and for Ads.

env.name: X_API_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth2 client secret, for a confidential client.

env.name: X_API_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: Loopback OAuth callback. Per-profile, or two profiles race for one port — and the URL must be registered with the X app.

env.name: X_API_TOKEN_FILE
env.description: Where the user token is stored. Per-profile, or two accounts share one login.

env.name: X_API_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: X_API_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD
env.description: Spend ceiling. X bills per read, so this is a real safety control, not a preference.

env.name: X_API_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables posting through the API rather than returning an intent URL.

env.name: X_ADS_ENABLED
env.description: Registers the Ads API tools. Needs a user context.

env.name: X_ADS_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables campaign mutations. No effect without X_ADS_ENABLED.

notes: Two write gates, not one: X_API_ALLOW_WRITES governs posting and
X_ADS_ALLOW_WRITES governs spending money. The manifest names the
first as the gate because that is the one the Activity window badges;
the second is an ordinary env entry that a profile sets deliberately.
X_API_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD is here for the same reason a write gate is:
on this API a read has a price, so an unbounded profile is a bill.

servers.summary: TastyTrade brokerage API: accounts, positions, balances, quotes, and order entry.

env.name: TASTYTRADE_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth client secret.

env.name: TASTYTRADE_REFRESH_TOKEN
env.description: Long-lived refresh token. This is the credential that can move money.

env.name: TASTYTRADE_ENV
env.description: prod or cert. cert is the sandbox, and the right default for a first profile.

env.name: TASTYTRADE_SCOPE
env.description: OAuth scope. Defaults to `read trade`; narrow it to `read` for a read-only profile.

env.name: TASTYTRADE_ALLOW_TRADING
env.description: Enables order entry. The highest-consequence gate in the manifest.

notes: The reason write gates are per-profile rather than global. One
tastytrade/cert profile with trading on and one tastytrade/prod
profile with trading off is a sane setup; a single global switch
makes it unexpressible.

servers.summary: BoursoBank customer API: accounts, transactions, statements, market data.

env.name: BOURSOBANK_CLIENT_NUMBER
env.description: Customer number used to log in.

env.name: BOURSOBANK_PASSWORD
env.description: Login password. Omit to log in interactively instead.

env.name: BOURSOBANK_SESSION_PATH
env.description: Where the authenticated session is cached. Per-profile.

env.name: BOURSOBANK_DOCUMENTS_DIR
env.description: Where downloaded statements land. Per-profile.

env.name: BOURSOBANK_ALLOW_TRADING
env.description: Enables order entry on the linked brokerage account.

notes: Logs in through a real browser session and needs MFA, so a profile of
this server is not merely credentials — it is a live session with a
timeout. The supervisor's idle-stop policy has to account for that.
The session cache is not a secret in the Keychain sense but it is
bearer-equivalent while it lasts, which is why it is stateEnv.

servers.summary: Buzzberg market intelligence: speaker calls, timelines and crowd sentiment.

env.name: BUZZBERG_BROWSER_CHANNEL
env.description: Browser channel to drive, e.g. chrome. Defaults to chrome.

env.name: BUZZBERG_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH
env.description: Explicit browser binary, when the channel cannot be found.

env.name: BUZZBERG_BROWSER_HEADLESS
env.description: Run the browser headless. On by default.

notes: Holds no credential at all — it drives a browser. It is in the
manifest for supervision and audit, not for secret storage, and it is
the one entry that proves those two jobs are separable.
It also spawns a browser, so its memory cost is unlike every other
entry here. Idle-stop matters more for this one than for any other.

servers.summary: Yahoo Finance market data: quotes, fundamentals, holders, time series.

env.name: YAHOO_FINANCE_COOKIE
env.description: Session cookie, when the anonymous crumb flow is being refused.

env.name: YAHOO_FINANCE_CRUMB
env.description: Matching crumb for the cookie above.

env.name: YAHOO_FINANCE_CONCURRENCY
env.description: Parallel requests. Defaults to 4.

notes: Read-only and normally credential-free: the cookie and crumb are a
fallback for when the anonymous path is throttled. Marked secret
anyway, because a session cookie is a session cookie.
